In the refuge of the Saadhs the dear Lord is found, and (there) we sing the Lord's praises every day.
May the dust of the devotees touch my mind and body, O dear Lord; (by it) all the fallen are made pure.
The fallen become pure in the company of those who have found the Creator.
Imbued with the Naam, they are givers of (spiritual) life; they give every day, and (their gifts) grow ever more.
Riddhis and siddhis (wealth and miraculous powers) and the nine treasures (come to) those who, repeating (the Name of) the Lord, have conquered their own self.
Nanak prays: the Saadhs, friends and companions, are found by great good fortune.
O dear Lord, they who have dealt in the True (Name) are bankers of full wealth.
O dear Lord, a great treasure is with them; the Lord's Kirtan is (their) profit.
Lust, anger and greed do not grip those who are imbued with God.
They know the One, they acknowledge the One, intoxicated with the love of the Lord.
Holding to the feet of the Sant (the Guru), they have taken refuge; their minds are full of eager longing.
Nanak prays: those who hold the Naam in their keeping, they alone are the true bankers.
O Nanak, one should remember that dear Lord alone whose power is set in all (creation).
Through the Guru, the dear Lord, the Creator, the all-pervading Being, Murari, does not slip from the mind.
Pain, disease and fear do not grip those who have meditated on the Lord, Har Har.
By the Sant's grace they have crossed the world-ocean; they have received what was written (for them) before.
Songs of rejoicing ring out, peace has come into the mind; the boundless Being has been met.
Nanak prays: remembering the Lord, Har Har, my wish has been fulfilled. ॥4॥
544.1: Raag Bihagra, Ghar 2, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); realised through the Guru's grace.
Grow longer, O dear night of joy, for love for my Beloved has taken hold (of me).
Grow less, O painful sleep, that I may touch his feet for ever.
I yearn for the dust of his feet and ever beg (for it); in the relish of the Naam I am detached (from the world).
Dyed in the love of my Beloved, intoxicated with Sahaj, I have cast off the great evil-mindedness.
Seizing my arm, he has made me his own; I am steeped in love; union with the Beloved is the true path.
Nanak prays: show grace, (O God), that I may stay attached to your feet.
O my friends and dear companions, let us hold to God's feet.
In my mind is great love for the Beloved; let us beg for devotion to the Lord.
Devotion to the Lord is found and God is meditated on when one goes and meets the Lord's servants.
Let pride, attachment and vice be given up, offering (him) this body, wealth and mind.
The Lord is the great Being, perfect, complete in every virtue; meeting him, let us break down the wall of doubt.
Nanak prays: hear (my) counsel, O friend: let us repeat the Lord's Name ever, ever, ever.
The Lord's bride is happily wed; she enjoys every delight.
She never sits as a widow, for God, (her Husband), is the everlasting Being.
She suffers no pain and meditates on God; blessed and most fortunate are such (brides).
They rest in peace and Sahaj and rid themselves of sins; they stay awake in the relish and love of the Naam.
They live united in love; the Lord's Name is their adornment; the Beloved's words are sweet and dear to them.
Nanak prays: they have obtained their heart's wish; they have met the Lord, the everlasting Being.
In that home are songs of joy, wonders and bliss,
(the home of one) in whose mind and body God, (the Lord of) supreme bliss, pervades.
The Lord, the Husband, is infinite and merciful; he is Sridhar (the Lord), Gobind, the uplifter of the fallen.
God, the Lord Murari, has shown grace, he who carries (us) across the fearsome world-ocean.
Whoever comes to his refuge, he hugs close: this is the Master's age-old way.
Nanak prays: the Lord, the Husband, ever at play, has been met. ॥4॥
544.2: Raag Bihagra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Lord's feet are a sacred pool: make your dwelling there, O mind.
Bathe in the Lord's pool, O mind, and all sins are destroyed.
Bathe there always; Gobind, the friend, destroys pain and darkness.
Birth and death do not befall that one; (Gobind) cuts away the nooses of Jam.
Join the Saadh Sangat, in love with the Naam; there every hope is fulfilled.
Nanak prays: show grace, O Lord, that I may dwell at your lotus feet.
There are bliss and delight, and ever the soft ringing of the unstruck (Anhad) melody.
Gathered together, the Sants sing the praise and victory of God.
Together the Sants sing and are pleasing to the Master, drenched in the relish and colour of the Lord's love.
They have gained the Lord as their profit and erased their self-conceit; long separated, they have met (him).
The One God, inaccessible and infinite, has taken them by the arm and shown them mercy.
Nanak prays: (they are) ever pure, and the true Shabad rings within (them) in sweet melody.
O fortunate one, listen to the Lord's Amrit Bani.
It comes to dwell in the heart of each one for whom it is written by (his) grace.
They alone have known the story of the Indescribable, on whom God himself shows grace.
Such a one has become immortal and does not die again; strife, anguish and pain are taken away.
He has found the Lord's refuge and does not forsake it to go (elsewhere); God's love is dear to his mind and body.
Nanak prays: let the pure Amrit Bani be sung for ever.
Mind and body have become absorbed (in him); nothing can be said (of it).
The One from whom (the soul) sprang has absorbed it into himself.
One with God's light like warp and weft, (it) has merged as water merges in water.
The One pervades water, land and sky; no other is seen.
He wholly fills the forests, the blades of grass and the three worlds; his worth cannot be told.
Nanak prays: he himself knows, who has fashioned this making. ॥4॥
545.1: Raag Bihagra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Sants go about searching for God, the support of life.
Without meeting the Beloved, (their) strength and body have wasted away.
O beloved God, meet (me) in your kindness; show compassion and attach (me) to the hem of your robe.
Give (me) your Name, O Master, that I may repeat it; beholding the sight of the Lord, one lives.
O all-powerful, all-pervading, ever unmoving, lofty, unreachable and infinite (God).
Nanak prays: show grace and meet (me), O Beloved, dear as life.
Recitations, austerities and fasts have been performed to behold the (Lord's) feet,
yet without the Master's refuge the burning (within) is quenched nowhere.
O God, (I have come) to your refuge; cut (my) fetters and carry (me) across the world-ocean.
I am without support and without virtue, and I know nothing; do not weigh my merits and faults.
O Gopal, merciful to the meek, Beloved, all-powerful, doer and cause of all,
Nanak, a chatrik, begs for the Lord's drop (of rain); meditating on the feet of the Lord, Har Har, I live.
The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is a pool of Amrit: drink of it.
It is found in the company of the Sants; repeating it, every task is fulfilled.
May the Lord, who fulfils all tasks and destroys pain, never slip from the mind, even for the blink of an eye.
(He is) bliss night and day, ever true; all virtues are in the Lord of the world.
The Master is beyond count, lofty and infinite; his abode is beyond reach.
Nanak prays: my wish is fulfilled; I have met Sri Rang (the Lord).
Those who hear and sing (the Lord's praise) gain the fruit of many millions of sacrificial rites.
Repeating the Name of the Lord, Har Har, they carry all their generations across.
Repeating the Lord's Name, mortals become beautiful; how far can I count their glory?
O Lord, dear as life, never slip from (our) minds; (they) ever dwell in their minds on your sight.
Blessed days have come: God, lofty, unreachable and infinite, has taken (them) and hugged (them) close.
Nanak prays: everything has borne fruit; God, most dear, has been met. ॥4॥
546.1: Raag Bihagra, a Chhant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Why are you steeped in what is other (than God)? The road (ahead) is full of pain.
O doer of sins, no one is your friend.
No one will be your friend; you will regret it for ever.
You do not repeat Gopal's virtues with your tongue; when will these days come again?
Leaves parted from the tree are not joined (to it again); on the road of Jam (the soul) goes alone.
Nanak prays: without the Lord's Name (the soul) wanders ever in misery.
You practise deceit in hiding, but the Knower knows all.
When Dharam Raj takes the account, (sinners) are crushed like sesame seeds in the oil-press.
For the deeds you have done, O mortal, endure the pain; you have been made to wander through countless births.
Steeped in the great enchantress (Maya), you have wasted this jewel of a life.
Except in the Name of the one Lord, (the soul) is clever in every other task.
Nanak prays: such is the writ written (for her): she is caught in doubt and attachment.
No one intercedes (for him): the ungrateful one is separated (from the Lord).
Jam's servant, utterly merciless, has come and seized him.
Seized, he is driven off (to reap) what he himself earned, steeped in the great enchantress.
Through the Guru he did not repeat Govind's virtues; (now) he is made to hug the red-hot pillars.
Robbed by lust, anger and pride, he has lost (his) understanding and repents.
Nanak prays: by the lot written (for him) he went astray, and did not repeat the Lord's Name with his tongue.
O God, apart from you there is no one who can save.
O Lord, to uplift the fallen is your age-old way.
O uplifter of the fallen, O Master, treasure of grace, merciful one, (I have come) to your refuge.
Lift (me) out of the blind well (of Maya), O Creator, cherisher of every heart.
(I am) in your refuge: cut my heavy fetters, and give (me) the one Name as (my) support.
Nanak prays: give (me) your hand and save (me), O Gobind, merciful to the meek.
That day is counted fruitful when one is united with the Lord God.
All comforts have appeared, and pains have fled far away.
Peace, Sahaj, bliss and delight abide for ever (when) Gopal's virtues are sung every day.
Meditate (on him) in the Saadh Sangat, joining in love, and one does not run through births again.
He has taken (me) and hugged (me) close, in Sahaj and in love; the primal shoot has sprung up.
Nanak prays: (God) himself has come to meet (me); one wanders nowhere else again. ॥5॥
547.1: Raag Bihagra, a Chhant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Hear my prayers, my Master.
Though filled with millions of wrongs, we are still your servants.
O remover of pain, bestower of mercy, enchanter of the mind, destroyer of strife and suffering,
I am in your refuge; keep my (honour), O all-pervading, stainless Lord.
Hearing and seeing, you are with all, O God, nearer than the nearest.
O Master, hear Nanak's prayer: save the servant of your house.
You are ever all-powerful; we are poor beggars.
I am sunk in attachment to Maya; pull me out, O Murari.
Bound by greed, attachment and vice, I commit countless wrongs.
The Creator is untouched and free of bonds; (we) reap what we ourselves have done.
Show kindness, O purifier of the fallen; I am worn out from wandering through many births.
Nanak prays: I am the servant of the Lord God, the support of soul and breath.
You are all-powerful and great; my understanding is slight.
You sustain even the ungrateful; your gaze is perfect.
O infinite Creator, unfathomable to understanding, I, the lowly one, know nothing.
Casting away the jewel, I gather cowrie shells, a lowly, ignorant beast.
(Maya,) utterly fickle, which forsakes (us) and goes, I have amassed by sinning again and again.
Nanak has come to your refuge, O all-powerful Master: keep my honour.
He from whom I was parted has himself brought me back to him;
in the company of the Saadh (the Guru), I have sung the Lord's praises.
As I sing ever the sublime praises of Govind, the Lord who is all bliss has become manifest.
With God, the bed (of my heart) has become beautiful; God has made me his own.
Leaving anxiety, I have become free of care, and have known pain no more.
Nanak lives by beholding (his) sight, having sung of Govind, the treasure of virtues. ॥4॥
547.2: Raag Bihagra, a Chhant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Speak, dear one of true dharma; why have you kept silent?
You have seen with your own eyes that the dealer in Maya departs (leaving it all).
Nothing goes with you except the Name of Gobind.
Lands, robes, gold and silver: all these pursuits are empty.
Sons, wife and worldly glory do not go with you; elephants and horses lead only to vice.
Nanak prays: without the Saadh Sangat, all that is of the world is false.
O king, why are you asleep, heavy with sleep? Why do you not wake?
False is the weeping for Maya; so many wail (for it).
So many wail for the great enchantress (Maya); without the Lord's Name there is no peace.
Thousands of clever tricks and devices (people) try, and are worn out; they go where (the Lord) wills.
In the beginning, the end and the middle he is all-pervading; he is everywhere, in every heart.
Nanak prays: those who have the Saadh Sangat go home with honour.
O king, you are held fast, taking (these) clever servants to be your own;
(but) from them you must surely part; those enticed (by them) repent.
Seeing the city of Harichand, you have gone astray; how can a lasting place be found (there)?
Without the Lord's Name, caught in other things of the creation, this precious birth is wasted.
Crying I, I, (one's) thirst is not quenched, nor are desires fulfilled, nor does wisdom come.
Nanak prays: without the Lord's Name, so many have gone away repenting.
In his grace (the Lord) has made you his own;
taking (you) by the arm he has pulled (you) out, and has given (you) the company of the Saadh.
As (you) worship the Lord in the Saadh Sangat, every sin and sorrow is burnt away.
This is the highest dharma, the true giving, the (right) deed; these go with you.
(Your) tongue worships the one Master; in the Lord's Name (your) mind and body are soaked.
O Nanak, whomever the Lord unites (with himself) becomes skilled in every virtue. ॥4॥
548.1: Bihagre ki Vaar: by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Peace is found by serving the Guru; do not look for peace anywhere else.
When the mind is pierced through by the Guru's Shabad, it dwells ever with the Lord.
O Nanak, the Naam is received by those alone on whom the Lord looks with his glance of grace. ॥1॥
548.2: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The treasure of praise is (his) gift; the one to whom he gives it spends it and eats of it.
Without the True Guru it never comes into one's hands; all are worn out with their rituals.
O Nanak, the manmukh world is without (this) wealth; hungry in the world beyond, what will it eat? ॥2॥
548.3: All is yours, you are everyone's; you created all.
You are at work in all; all have meditated on you.
You accept the devotion of the one who is pleasing to your mind.
What pleases the Lord God, that comes to be; all act as you make them act.
Praise the Lord, the greatest of all, who has always kept the honour of his Sants. ॥1॥
548.4: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O Nanak, the one with (true) wisdom has conquered the world; everyone (else) the world has conquered.
Through the Naam (his) task is fulfilled; whatever happens comes about in Sahaj.
Through the Guru's teaching (his) understanding is unshakeable; no one can make it waver.
The Lord takes the side of his devotees, and (their) work turns out well.
(The Lord) has led the manmukhs astray from the Root itself; within them are craving, greed and pride.
Their time passes night and day in quarrels; they do not reflect through the Shabad.
The Creator has robbed them of sense and understanding; all they speak is corrupt.
No gift whatever satisfies them; within them is great thirst, ignorance and darkness.
O Nanak, it is better to break with the manmukhs, whose love is attachment to Maya. ॥1॥
549.1: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Those who have the True Guru and the Creator over their heads: what can fear and anxiety do to them?
From the very beginning he keeps their honour; he himself is the protector.
Meeting the Beloved, they have found peace, reflecting on the True Shabad.
O Nanak, they have served the Giver of peace, who himself is the assayer. ॥2॥
549.2: All beings and creatures are yours; you are the wealth of all.
The one you give to receives everything; there is no other rival beside you.
You alone are the Giver of all; to you, the Lord, (all) pray.
Whosever (prayer) pleases you, you grant; that servant is acclaimed.
All this is your play at work; pain and pleasure rest with you. ॥2॥
549.3: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The Gurmukhs are pleasing to the True One; at the True One's door they are found true.
Bliss fills the minds of these friends (of the Lord); they reflect on the Guru's Shabad.
They have enshrined the Shabad within; the Creator has cut away (their) pain and made light (in them).
O Nanak, the Protector will protect (them), showing his grace. ॥1॥
549.4: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
(If one) serves and works for the Guru, doing the task steeped in (God's) fear,
(then) as is the One he serves, so does he become, if he walks in his will.
O Nanak, everything is he himself; there is no other, no second place. ॥2॥
549.5: Only you know your greatness; there is none other as great as you.
Were there another rival as great as you, one could speak of him; as great as you, you alone are.
Whoever has served you has found peace; how can anyone else match him?
You are able to break and to make, and you are the Giver; all stand before you with joined palms, to beg.
I see no giver as great as you; you have given gifts to all, in the continents, the universes, the netherworlds, the realms and all the worlds. ॥3॥
549.6: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
(If) faith has not come into the mind, and love has not taken hold in Sahaj,
(if) the taste of the Shabad has not been found, what praises can (one) sing by the mind's stubbornness?
O Nanak, approved is the coming (into the world) of one who, through the Guru, merges in the True One. ॥1॥
549.7: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The fool does not recognise his own self; he hurts others with what he says.
His nature from the start has not left (him); the blind one, separated (from the Lord), suffers blows.
He has not been broken and reshaped in the fear of the True Guru, that he might stay merged in (the Lord's) embrace.
Night and day his anxiety never ends; without the Shabad he suffers pain.
Lust, anger and greed are strong within him; (his life) passes in endless worldly business.
Feet, hands, sight and hearing are worn out; his days are spent, and (the end) has drawn near.
He has found no sweetness in the True Name, through which the nine treasures are gained.
If one dies while living, and after that death lives again, then one attains liberation.
The mortal has not received (God's) grace from the very beginning; without grace, what can he gain?
Cherish the Guru's Shabad, you fool; liberation and understanding are found through the Shabad.
O Nanak, one finds the True Guru only when one sheds the self from within. ॥2॥
550.1: Why should one in whose mind my Master dwells be anxious about anything?
The Lord is the giver of comfort in all things; why turn one's face from meditating on him, even for a moment, an instant?
One who has meditated on the Lord has gained every blessing; let us go daily to the company of the Sants, sit, and join with them face to face.
All the sorrows, hungers and ills of the Lord's servant are gone; all the bonds of (such) a servant are broken.
Through the Lord's grace one becomes a devotee of the Lord; through the sight of the faces of the Lord's devotees the whole world ought to cross over. ॥4॥
550.2: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
May that tongue burn which has not found the taste of the Lord.
O Nanak, that tongue is steeped in the Shabad which has enshrined the Lord, Har Har, in the mind. ॥1॥
550.3: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
May that tongue burn which has forgotten the Lord's Name.
O Nanak, through the Guru the tongue repeats (the Name of) the Lord, and loves the Lord's Name. ॥2॥
550.4: The Lord is himself the Master, himself the servant and devotee; the Lord himself acts, and makes (all) act.
The Lord himself watches and is glad; he himself sets (each) to what pleases him.
The Lord puts some on the path; the Lord himself sends some into the wilderness.
The Lord is the true Master, and true is his justice; having made all his plays, he watches them.
Servant Nanak, through the Guru's grace, says (this), and sings the praises of the True Lord. ॥5॥
550.5: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Only some rare dervish knows (the way of) the dervish.
If he roams from house to house, begging, cursed is his life and cursed his garb.
If he lays aside hope and anxiety, and through the Guru takes the Name as alms,
his feet are to be washed; I, Nanak, am a sacrifice to him. ॥1॥
550.6: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O Nanak, there is a tree with one fruit, and two birds (sit on it).
They are not seen coming or going, and these birds have no wings.
(One) has tasted pleasures of many colours; (the other) stays free of desire through the Shabad.
O Nanak, those steeped in the fruit, the essence of the Lord, bear by (his) grace the true mark. ॥2॥
550.7: He himself is the earth, and he himself the ploughman; he himself makes (the grain) grow, and has it ground.
He himself cooks; he himself gives the dishes and serves; he himself sits down and eats.
He himself gives the water; he himself gives the toothpick, and he himself has (water) taken in the palm to rinse the mouth.
He himself calls the company and seats it, and he himself bids (it) farewell.
On whom the Lord is merciful, him he himself makes accept his Hukam. ॥6॥
551.1: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Rites and religious duties are all bonds; sin and merit too are ties (that bind one to the world).
Possessiveness and attachment are bonds as well; son and wife, too, are an entanglement.
Wherever I look, there is a rope: the tie of Maya.
O Nanak, without the True Name the blind (person) is taken up only with the dealings (of the world). ॥1॥
551.2: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Light comes to the blind (person) only when, by (God's) will, the True Guru meets him.
(Then) he snaps (Maya's) bonds and abides in the True One, and the darkness of ignorance leaves him.
He sees all things as his alone who shaped and made the body.
O Nanak, (he stays) in the Creator's refuge, and the Creator keeps his honour. ॥2॥
551.3: When the Creator himself sat and shaped the frame (of the world), he asked counsel of no second servant.
What then could anyone take, or anyone give, when he had made no other, no second one?
Then the Creator himself brought forth the world, and gave his gift to all.
He himself set up (the way of) his service, and he himself, through the Guru, drank the Amrit (of the Name).
He himself is the Formless One, and he himself is form; whatever he does, that alone comes about. ॥7॥
551.4: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The Gurmukhs serve the ever-true God night and day, in Sahaj and in love.
Ever in bliss they sing the virtues of the True One, keeping in their hearts him who pervades below and above.
The Beloved has come to dwell within them; the Creator wrote (his) grace (for them) from the very beginning.
O Nanak, (God) has united them (with himself), showing his grace of his own accord. ॥1॥
551.5: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
(God) is not found by saying and describing, even if one goes on singing (his) virtues always, night and day.
Without (his) grace no one has found him; (many) have died barking and wailing.
Through the Guru's Shabad mind and body are drenched (in love), and (God) himself comes to dwell in the mind.
O Nanak, (God) is found through (his) glance of grace; he himself unites (one) with himself. ॥2॥
551.6: He himself is the Vedas, the Puranas and all the Shastras; he himself expounds them, and he himself is moved (hearing them).
The Creator himself sits and worships, and he himself spreads out the expanse (of the world).
He himself is engaged in the world, and he himself is withdrawn from it; he himself tells of the One who cannot be told.
He himself has all good deeds done, and he himself stays untouched (by them).
The Creator himself gives pleasure and pain, and he himself bestows forgiveness. ॥8॥
551.7: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O Sheikh, give up (the habit of) force within you; keep the fear (of God), and be rid of your madness.
Through the fear of the Guru so many have been carried across; in that fear one finds the Fearless One.
Pierce your hard mind with the Shabad, and peace will come to dwell in (your) mind.
The work done in peace: that is what the Master accepts.
Says Nanak: no one has found (God) through lust and anger; go and ask any man of wisdom. ॥1॥
551.8: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The manmukh is attached to Maya; no love for the Naam takes hold (of him).
He practises falsehood, hoards falsehood, and makes falsehood his food.
(The manmukhs) die heaping up the wealth of Maya, which is poison, and in the end it all turns to ashes.
They perform rites and religious duties, ritual purity and self-restraint, (but) within them is greed, (and) vice.
O Nanak, whatever the manmukh does is not accepted; in the Lord's court he is put to shame. ॥2॥
552.1: He himself makes the sources of life, he himself (their) speech, and he himself the continents and the universes.
He himself is the ocean, he himself the sea, and he himself has set the jewels within it.
He himself lets (the jewels) be found by the one on whom he shows grace, the one whom the Lord makes Gurmukh.
He himself is the terrifying world-ocean, he himself the ship; he himself is the boatman, and he himself crosses over.
The Creator himself does and causes all to be done; (O Lord,) there is no other, no second, equal to you. ॥9॥
552.2: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Service of the True Guru bears fruit, if one does it with the mind attuned.
(By it) the treasure of the Naam is gained, and the Lord who is free of care comes to dwell in the mind.
The pain of birth and death is cut away, and Haumai and possessiveness depart.
The highest state is attained, and one remains merged in the True One.
O Nanak, those for whom it was written from the past: the True Guru has come and met them. ॥1॥
552.3: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The True Guru is steeped in the Naam; in Kalyug he becomes the ship.
Whoever becomes Gurmukh reaches the far shore: (Gurmukhs are) those within whom that True One dwells.
He cherishes the Naam, gathers the Naam, and through the Naam alone has honour.
O Nanak, when the True Guru is found, (the Naam) is attained by (God's) grace. ॥2॥
552.4: He himself is the philosopher's stone, he himself the metal, and he himself has turned (it) into gold.
He himself is the Master, he himself the servant, and he himself the destroyer of sins.
The Lord himself enjoys (the world) through every body, and all the collyrium (the dark of Maya) is himself too.
He himself is discernment, he himself the knower of all; he himself, through the Guru, breaks (the bonds of Maya).
Your servant Nanak never has enough of praising you, O Creator; you, Lord, are the giver of peace, the greatest of all. ॥10॥
552.5: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Without serving the True Guru, all the deeds (beings) do become the soul's bonds.
Without serving the True Guru they find no resting place; they die and are born again, and come and go.
Without serving the True Guru (one's) speech is insipid, and the Naam does not come into the mind to dwell.
O Nanak, without serving the True Guru they are tied up and beaten in the city of Jam, and rise and depart (from the world) with blackened faces. ॥1॥
552.6: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Some serve the True Guru and wait on him, and love for the Lord's Name takes hold of them.
O Nanak, they set their own lives right, and bring deliverance to their families too. ॥2॥
552.7: He himself is the school, he himself the teacher, and he himself brings the pupils to learn.
He himself is father and mother, and it is he who makes the children wise.
In one place he himself reads and understands everything; in another he himself makes (them) ignorant.
Some he calls within (his) mansion, when they please your own mind, O True One.
Those to whom he himself gives glory through the Guru: those people are known in the true court. ॥11॥
553.1: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji), addressed to Mardana.
The temper of Kalyug is the still, lust is the wine, and the mind is the one who drinks it.
Anger is the cup, filled with attachment, and pride is the one who pours.
The gathering is one of false greed; drinking and drinking, (the mind) is ruined.
Make good conduct the mash and truthfulness the molasses, and make the True (Name) the finest wine.
Make virtues the bread, gentleness the ghee, and modesty the meat: (let this be your) food.
O Nanak, (this food) is obtained through the Guru; eating it, the vices depart. ॥1॥
553.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji), addressed to Mardana.
The body is the mash, self-conceit the wine, and the restless running of craving the gathering.
Desire is the cup, filled with falsehood, and Jamkaal (death) makes them drink.
O Nanak, by drinking this wine many vices are earned.
(Let) knowledge (of God) be the molasses, (his) praise the bread, and (his) fear the meat: (let this be the) food;
(then,) O Nanak, this food is true; the True Name is the support (of life). ॥2॥
553.3: (If) the body is the mash, (knowing) the self the wine, and its stream is Amrit,

(if the gathering) is union with the Sat Sangat (the company of the true), and the cup is loving attunement (to God), filled with Amrit, (then) drinking and drinking it, people cut away their vices. ॥3॥
553.4: He himself is gods, men, ganas (Shiva's attendants) and gandharvas (heavenly singers); he himself is the word of the six darshanas (the six schools of philosophy).
He himself is Shiva, Shankar and Mahesh; he himself, through the Guru, (tells) the story of the Indescribable.
He himself is the yogi, he himself the man of pleasures; he himself (as) the sanyasi roams the wilderness.
He holds discourse with himself, he himself instructs; he himself is skilled, beautiful and wise.
He stages his own play and watches it himself; he himself is the knower of all beings. ॥12॥
553.5: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
That sandhya (the prayer at the junctures of the day) alone is accepted, through which my Lord God comes into the mind,
love for the Lord wells up, and (which) burns away attachment to Maya.
By the Guru's grace duality dies, the mind is stilled, and (one) makes reflection (on God) one's sandhya.
O Nanak, the manmukh performs the sandhya, (but) his mind does not settle; he dies and is born, and is ruined. ॥1॥
553.6: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Crying out, Beloved, Beloved, I wandered over the whole world, yet my thirst would not leave me.
O Nanak, on meeting the True Guru my thirst has gone; coming home, I have found my Husband Lord. ॥2॥
553.7: He himself is the thread (the soul) and the supreme thread (God); all is himself; the Master himself has become the servant.
He himself created the eighteen castes; he himself is Brahm, and he himself has taken the rule (of creation).
He himself kills and he himself lets go; he himself forgives and shows mercy.
He himself is unerring and never errs; all (his) judgement is true, and truth alone prevails.
Those to whom he himself gives understanding through the Guru: from within them the wandering of duality has gone. ॥13॥
553.8: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Those who do not remember the Lord's Name in the Saadh Sangat: dust flies over their bodies.
(Such a body) does not know the One who made it; O Nanak, shame on (such) a body without the salt (of love). ॥1॥
554.1: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(The body in whose) heart (God's) lotus feet dwell, (and whose) tongue repeats (the Name of) Gopal,
O Nanak, (the body through which) that God is remembered: cherish that body. ॥2॥
554.2: The Creator himself is the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage, and he himself takes the bath (at them).
The Lord himself lives by self-discipline, and he himself makes (beings) repeat the Naam.
The destroyer of fear himself becomes merciful, and he himself gives every gift.
The one to whom (God) himself gives understanding through the Guru ever receives honour in the Lord's court.
The one whose honour the Lord, the Master, keeps: that servant of the Lord is (one with) the True One. ॥14॥
554.3: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O Nanak, the world is blind without meeting the True Guru, and does blind deeds.
It does not attune its mind to the Shabad, through which peace would come to dwell in the mind.
Clinging to the darkness of tamas, it wanders ever; its days and nights pass in burning.
Whatever pleases him comes to pass; nothing (about it) can be said. ॥1॥
554.4: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The True Guru has commanded: do this work;
by way of the Guru's door, cherish the Master (in your hearts).
The Master is ever present; cut away the film of doubt (from your eyes), and enshrine (his) light within.
The Lord's Name is Amrit: apply this medicine.
Keep the True Guru's will in your minds, and (make) true love your regimen.
Says Nanak: (this medicine) will keep you in peace here, and hereafter you will rejoice with the Lord. ॥2॥
554.5: He himself is the eighteen loads of vegetation (all plant life), and it is he who makes it bear fruit.
He is himself the gardener, he himself waters it all, and he himself puts (the fruit) into the mouth.
He himself is the doer and he himself the enjoyer; he himself gives, and has (others) give.
He himself is the Master, he himself the protector, and he himself pervades (all).
Servant Nanak tells the greatness of the Lord, the Creator, who has not a sesame seed's worth of greed. ॥15॥
554.6: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
One person brings (a vessel) filled (with wine); another comes and fills (his cup from it).
Drinking it, the understanding goes far away and madness comes in;
one no longer knows one's own from another's, and is thrust away by the Master.
Drinking it, the Master is forgotten, and punishment is met in the Lord's court:
(such) false wine should never be drunk at all, so far as it lies in one's power.
O Nanak, through (God's) glance of grace the true wine is received by the one whom the True Guru comes to meet.
(He) stays ever in the Master's love, and finds a place in (the Lord's) mansion. ॥1॥
554.7: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
When understanding comes to this world, it dies while living.
When he (God) has put it to sleep, it stays asleep; when he wakes it, then it comes to its senses.
O Nanak, if he casts his own glance of grace, he himself unites (it) with the True Guru.
(Then) by the Guru's grace (it) dies while living, and after that there is no dying again. ॥2॥
554.8: The One by whose doing everything comes to pass is beholden to no one.
Everyone, O Lord, eats what you give; all are dependent on you.
Whoever praises you gains everything: the one on whom the Stainless One's grace rests.
That one alone is the banker and the true trader who has taken on the cargo, the wealth of your Name, O Lord.
Praise him, all of you, O Sants, who has struck down and scattered the heap of the love of another. ॥16॥
555.1: O Kabir, dying and dying, the whole world has died, yet no one knows even how to die.
One who dies such a death will not die again. ॥1॥
555.2: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
What can I know of how we shall die, or what our dying will be like?
If the Master does not slip from the mind, then dying is easy.
The world is afraid of death; everyone wants to go on living.
One who, by the Guru's grace, dies while living understands (God's) Hukam.
O Nanak, one who dies such a death has life for ever. ॥2॥
555.3: When the Lord, the Master, himself turns merciful, the Lord himself has (one) repeat his own Name.
He himself unites (him) with the True Guru and gives peace; his own servant is dear to the Lord himself.
He himself guards the honour of his servants, and makes (others) bow at his devotees' feet.
Dharam Raj (too) is of the Lord's making; he does not come near the Lord's humble servant.
Whoever is dear to the Lord is dear to all; countless others come and go, wearing themselves out. ॥17॥
555.4: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The whole world goes about saying Ram, Ram, (yet so) Ram is not found.
He is inaccessible and beyond the reach of the senses, exceedingly great; no scale can hold him, he cannot be weighed.
No one has found his worth; he cannot be had from any place (at any price).
When (the mind) was pierced by the Guru's Shabad, in this way he came and dwelt in the mind.
O Nanak, he himself is beyond measure; by the Guru's grace (he is seen) pervading (all).
He himself is merged (in all) and stays merged; he himself has come and met (the seeker). ॥1॥
555.5: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O mind, this wealth is the Naam, through which there is peace for ever and ever.
No loss ever comes to it at all; there is always profit.
Though eaten and spent, it never runs short; he (God) goes on giving it for ever and ever.
(With it) there is no anxiety at all, and never any harm.
O Nanak, (this wealth) is found through the Guru, by the one on whom (God) casts his glance of grace. ॥2॥
555.6: He himself is inside every heart; he himself is also outside.
He himself is at work unseen; he himself is plain to see.
For thirty-six ages he made pitch darkness and abode in Sunn.
No Vedas, Puranas or Shastras were there; there was the Lord himself alone, Narhari (the Lord of men).
He sat in deep absorption, himself apart from all.
He alone knows his own measure; he himself is the fathomless ocean. ॥18॥
555.7: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The world has died in Haumai, and goes on dying and dying.
So long as there is breath within, it does not remember (the Lord); what will it do when it goes on ahead?
One who has wisdom stays awake; the ignorant one does the deeds of the blind.
O Nanak, what one earns here, that one receives; going on ahead, one obtains it. ॥1॥
556.1: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
From the very source the Master's Hukam has gone forth: without the True Guru, (he) cannot be remembered.
When the True Guru is met, (the Lord) is found pervading within, and (one) stays ever attuned (to him).
With every breath he keeps (the Lord) ever in mind; not one breath goes to waste.
The fear of birth and death is gone; (he) has attained the rank of true life.
O Nanak, (God) gives this rank to the one on whom, in his will, he shows grace. ॥2॥
556.2: He himself is the Knower and the Seer; he himself is the foremost.
He himself shows (his) forms; he himself becomes absorbed in meditation.
He himself goes about as a silent sage; he himself discourses on spiritual knowledge.
He tastes bitter to no one; he is pleasing to all.
His praise cannot be put into words; I am a sacrifice (to him) for ever and ever. ॥19॥
556.3: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
In Kalyug, O Nanak, (people) are born as jinns:
the son a little jinn, the daughter a little jinni, and the wife the chief of the jinns. ॥1॥
556.4: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The Hindus have utterly gone astray, and are going down the wrong path.
They perform the worship Narad told them of.
For these blind and mute ones there is pitch darkness.
Foolish and unlettered, they take up stones and worship them.
When they (the stones) sink of themselves, how can you cross over? ॥2॥
556.5: Everything is in your hands, (O God); you are the True Sovereign.
The devotees are dyed in the love of the One, and trust (him) fully.
The Lord's Name is the food of Amrit; (your) servants eat their fill of it.
(By it) all treasures are gained; Simran is the true profit.
The Sants are dear to the Supreme Lord; O Nanak, the Lord is inaccessible and unfathomable. ॥20॥
556.6: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Everything comes by (God's) Hukam alone; everything goes by Hukam alone.
If some fool thinks (it comes) from himself, he is blind and does the deeds of the blind.
O Nanak, it is a rare one who understands the Hukam through the Guru: the one on whom (God), in his will, shows grace. ॥1॥
556.7: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
That one is the yogi, and that one finds the (true) way of yoga, to whom the Naam comes through the Guru.
In the town (of the body) of that yogi, all (the virtues) dwell; by a holy garb, yoga does not come about.
O Nanak, rare is such a yogi, in whose heart (the Lord) becomes manifest. ॥2॥
556.8: He himself brought forth the creatures, and he himself is (their) support.
He himself is seen as the subtle, and he himself is the expanse (of the world).
He himself stays alone and apart; he himself is a vast family.
Nanak begs, O Lord, for the gift of the dust of the Sants' feet.
I can think of no other giver; you alone are the Giver.
